top_stories.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Affair Sparks Spy Investigation
points: Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang (a Singapore-linked executive, no relation), who U.S. intelligence and a Marco Rubio-overseen memo allege is connected to China's top intelligence agency.

Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation with outside lawyers; both the board and Huang say there's no evidence company secrets were compromised, and China denies all espionage allegations.
House Republicans demanded a closed-door congressional briefing, with deadlines cited around November 5th–12th; more investigations are expected.
Nvidia is keeping Huang as CEO during the review; the story raises national-security concerns since Huang controls the chip supply powering advanced AI.

unique_angles.point: Huang had previously called the meetings with Alice Huang 'completely normal' before admitting infidelity in a staff letter.
Alice Huang's company had faced prior accusations of smuggling Nvidia chips into China, and intelligence officials reportedly monitored the situation for about a year before public disclosure.

top_stories.title: Unreleased Anthropic Model Proves 18-Year-Old Quantum Computing Conjecture
points: Physical Superintelligence (PSI) used an unreleased Anthropic AI model to prove the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, unsolved since 2008, which concerns limits on quantum computers' advantage on 'messy' problems where no single data point dominates.

The proof was formally verified using Lean (a logic-checking tool that validates every step of a mathematical proof, preventing confident-sounding but incorrect reasoning), and PSI also published the conjecture's statement in Lean for public audit.

Four Stanford researchers who had solved a smaller version of the problem reviewed and praised the proof as a major result, though the wider mathematical community (including the conjecture's original namesakes) has not yet weighed in.

items.title: Anthropic's $3.4B Power Play for Gas Generators
points: Anthropic agreed to pay roughly $3.4 billion to OnePWR for 1.7 gigawatts of gas-fired power generators (enough capacity for about 1.4 million homes).
OnePWR had ordered the generators from Caterpillar two years prior but ran short on cash; Anthropic took over the existing order to skip the typical multi-year backlog for new generator orders.
The deal is based on a single unnamed source, and neither Anthropic nor OnePWR has publicly confirmed it.

items.title: Perplexity Launches 'Teammates' Agents
points: Perplexity's new Teammates feature, available to Max subscribers, provides persistent AI agents that handle ongoing tasks like research or bug triage.
Agents notify users via Slack when they need input, functioning more like long-term collaborators than one-off chatbot queries.

items.title: U.S. Job Market Resists AI Displacement Fears
points: U.S. employers added 70,000 professional and business services jobs in October despite widespread concern about AI-driven automation.
The data suggests white-collar job displacement from AI may not be as imminent as many had feared.

items.title: AI Safety Testing Center Shifts Reporting Line
points: The U.S. government's AI safety testing center began informally reporting to a White House office.
The center still lacks a permanent director.

items.title: Anthropic's Claude Gets a Memory 'Dreaming' System
points: Claude agents now use downtime to cross-check saved memory notes against past work logs, catching errors and reorganizing information—unlike ChatGPT's older approach of building static user profiles.
In Pokémon game tests, newer Claude models performed far better with fewer memory files: Sonnet 3.7 earned 4 badges using just 10 files versus an older Sonnet's 1 badge from 413 files.
Anthropic found that explaining to the AI *why* memory matters works better than giving it rigid rules about what to record.

items.title: Turning X Bookmarks into AI-Powered Research
points: Users can connect Grok Bot (bundled with X Premium/Ultra) and bookmark 8–12 posts on one topic—mixing examples, questions, and problems rather than just announcements.
The bot groups bookmarks into themes, checks claims against original posts with direct source links, and can draft a summary post from a chosen theme.
This reflects what an individual user has been reading, not a proof of broader sentiment across all of X.

items.title: Higgsfield Miracle: Layer-Based AI Video Editing
points: Higgsfield Miracle converts AI-generated video into editable layers, letting users adjust individual elements (objects, colors, speeds) in real time without regenerating the whole scene.
A viral demo (20M views) claims pixel-level editing capability (ability to modify individual image dots/color data).
Currently in private beta, with planned integration into ChatGPT (as a plugin) and Claude (via MCP, a standard protocol for connecting AI models to external tools).

items.title: Apple Pushes to Accelerate Siri Into an Autonomous Agent
points: Apple CEO-level exec John Ternus is pressing software chief Craig Federighi to move beyond incremental updates and make Siri an autonomous agent (software capable of completing multi-step tasks independently).
The redesigned Siri would compete directly with Meta Muse, OpenAI's reasoning-enabled ChatGPT, and Claude's agentic 'Duet' mode.
Potential launch as soon as 2027, though Apple has not committed to a firm timeline.

items.title: Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small Model Excels at Vision Tasks
points: Inkling 2 Small performs strongly on long-running tasks like coding, research, and office work, with standout results in vision (interpreting and analyzing images).
In a notable demo, it beat Thinking Machines' own researchers in a blind wine-tasting test, correctly identifying wines from photos 19 out of 20 times.
It's set to debut as a top open-weight model (publicly released model weights with no licensing restrictions) on the DesignArena leaderboard, with full weights releasing the following week.

sections.title: 1. The Anthropic Power Play: $3.4B for 1.7 Gigawatts
points: Anthropic agreed to pay OnePWR roughly $3.4 billion for 1.7 gigawatts (capacity to power ~1.4 million homes) of gas-fired generators.

OnePWR had ordered these generators from Caterpillar two years ago but lacked cash to complete payment; Anthropic took over the existing orders to avoid multi-year waits typical for new generator orders.
The deal comes from a single unnamed source and Reuters couldn't independently verify it; neither Anthropic nor OnePWR has publicly confirmed.

sections.title: 2. AI Solves 18-Year Quantum Puzzle With Formal Verification
points: Physical Superintelligence (PSI) used an unreleased Anthropic model to prove the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture—a mathematical problem unsolved since 2008 about the computational advantage of quantum computers.

The conjecture asks: on problems where every piece of data matters, must one piece matter much more than others? Proving 'yes' limits quantum computers' theoretical advantage on messy problems to needing roughly square-root extra work, not exponential.

PSI verified the proof using Lean, a logic verifier that checks every step and cannot be fooled by confident-sounding errors, then published the conjecture itself in Lean so others can audit the problem statement.

Four Stanford researchers who solved a smaller version reviewed the proof and called it a major result, but the broader mathematical community has not yet weighed in; comments from the conjecture's namesakes are not documented.

points: Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation after CEO Jensen Huang disclosed a personal relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, though Huang and the board have stated they see no evidence that company secrets were compromised.
The U.S. government's AI safety testing center began informally reporting to a White House office, though the center still lacks a permanent director.
